# AtomicWrite

A file being written to replace `target`, which appears under that name only when it is complete.

```rux
pub struct AtomicWrite {
    // private fields
}
```

Move-only. [`Commit`](/docs/api/filesystem/atomic-write#commit) syncs the contents and moves them onto the target; [`Abandon`](/docs/api/filesystem/atomic-write#abandon), or destroying the value,
deletes the partial file and leaves the target as it was. An early return therefore leaves the old contents
in place, which is the behavior that makes this worth using.

## Associated functions

<h3 id="begin"><code>Begin</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Begin(allocator: Allocator, target: Path) -> AtomicWrite ! IoError
```

Begins replacing `target`.
The temporary is created in the target's own directory, which is what keeps the final rename atomic. The
target need not exist; if it does, it is untouched until [`Commit`](/docs/api/filesystem/atomic-write#commit).

| Name        | Type        | Description                              |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from             |
| `target`    | `Path`      | the path the finished contents will take |

**Returns**: a write in progress against a temporary file

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Atomic.rux#L51)

## Methods

<h3 id="stream"><code>Stream</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Stream(self: &var AtomicWrite) -> FileStream
```

A stored writer over the partial file.
Only for a value that must keep the stream, such as a buffered writer. Writing to the replacement for the
duration of a call borrows the [`AtomicWrite`](/docs/api/filesystem/atomic-write) itself, which is a `Writer`.
The [`AtomicWrite`](/docs/api/filesystem/atomic-write) must outlive the result and must not be moved while it exists. See [`FileStream`](/docs/api/filesystem/file-stream).

**Returns**: a stream over the partial file, held by address

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Atomic.rux#L72)

<h3 id="commit"><code>Commit</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Commit(self: &var AtomicWrite, allocator: Allocator) -> ! IoError
```

Forces the contents to the device and moves them onto the target.
The sync happens **before** the rename, so the final name can never point at contents that never
arrived. Afterwards the target holds the new file and the temporary is gone; a reader that opened the
name at any moment saw the old file or the new one.
What this does not promise is that the directory entry survives a crash: that needs the containing
directory synced too, which Windows does not offer, so the guarantee stops at atomicity on every system
rather than being durable on some and pretending on the rest.

| Name        | Type        | Description                  |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from |

**Returns**: success when the target now holds the contents; on failure it still holds the old ones

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Atomic.rux#L93)

## Implements Writer

`AtomicWrite` conforms to `Writer`.

<h3 id="write"><code>Write</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Write(self: &var AtomicWrite, bytes: char8[..]) -> uint ! IoError
```

Writes into the partial file.
Writing to a replacement is what the type is for, so it is a `Writer` itself rather than something a caller
reaches a stream out of: `let sink: &var Writer = replacement;` borrows it, and nothing has to be kept alive
beside it.
One attempt, partial on purpose, exactly as the underlying file's is; `WriteAll` does the looping.

| Name    | Type        | Description      |
| ------- | ----------- | ---------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the run to write |

**Returns**: how much of it the file took

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Atomic.rux#L141)

<h3 id="flush"><code>Flush</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Flush(self: &var AtomicWrite) -> ! IoError
```

Flushes the partial file, which holds nothing back.
[`Commit`](/docs/api/filesystem/atomic-write#commit) is what makes the contents durable, and it syncs before it renames.

**Returns**: what the file reported

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Atomic.rux#L149)

## Destructor

```rux
func ~AtomicWrite(self: &var AtomicWrite)
```

Discards an uncommitted replacement, leaving the target untouched.
This is the property that makes the type worth using: an early return or a failure part-way through
writing leaves the old contents exactly where they were, with no partial file left behind.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Atomic.rux#L126)
